question.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $\mathbf b,$ given by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/9d0b186213211813b290f502888f68e0603bc9f77bcd7ea9d6262cb7449c00e7.svg)

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/4298fe244fd6c66c7623ad508c97b96464321387506aa1e4be5e2399a5c9a862.svg)

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 15 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 66\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=5 \\ 15{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=66.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $y_1=5$ and $y_2=-9.$ 

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/a86dfd0e07b8c415e526764cf9f7ba8f020609bf7b13cc90536deba868ec4aa6.svg)
